A1.justification: Despite retitling and substantial reorganization, both PDFs describe the same chat-model language-adaptation work. Their main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original adaptation experiments across three model families and seven target languages, including task performance, inference efficiency, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original adaptation results and adds Chat Vector comparisons, safety evaluations, and chat and reasoning experiments, including appendix results.

M1.justification: ElChat matches v1's primary Tmpl+Copy+Merge pipeline: vocabulary expansion, partial continual pre-training, chat-template prompting, special-token copying, and model merging. Training components and merging ratios remain unchanged. Merging every layer in v3 does not establish an effective change because the intermediate layers remain identical.

E1.justification: v3 adds target-language TruthfulQA, ToxiGen, and ImplicitHate; Global MMLU in four target languages; MGSM in Bengali and Telugu; and English GSM8K and MT-Bench. BBH is removed. The seven adaptation languages, MADLAD-400 training corpus, and core summarization, translation, and reading-comprehension coverage remain.

E2.justification: Chat Vector, absent from v1's evaluated comparators, becomes the central comparison method in v3. Conversely, v1's source/target merged-base comparator is removed. The original base, chat, vocabulary-expansion, and CPT-only baselines largely remain under simplified names.

E3.justification: The reported MT protocol changes from zero-shot to three-shot, and adapted chat baselines now use chat templates. Gemma 2 9B is removed from the experimental model set. New evaluations introduce multi-turn reasoning and LLM-judge protocols, including Likert-5 MT-Bench scoring. Core CPT budgets and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's template/copy/merge analyses across three model families become Llama 3.1 component-removal ablations covering chat and reasoning, including a new isolation of Merge's contribution. MGSM success and reasoning-failure examples replace the translation case studies. CPT-only, output-token, and language-specific analyses remain with revised comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run means for SUM and MT, single deterministic evaluations for other tasks, and 95% confidence intervals on aggregate plots. The added results do not establish changed run-count, seed-reporting, or statistical-estimation practices.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive CV, safety, chat, and reasoning results and removes Gemma 2 and BBH entries. MT values are replaced under revised conditions: Llama 3.1's proposed-method Amharic-to-English chrF is 3.8 in v1 Table 6 versus 27.5 in v3 Table 10, with different shot settings. The new target-task averages give ElChat three of eight wins over CV, inconsistent with Section 5.2's equal-win summary.

T1.justification: Neither version develops substantive theoretical results or proofs. v1's explicit vocabulary notation is condensed into procedural descriptions in v3 without changing the underlying mathematical construction. Newly described evaluation metrics do not introduce new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes the first investigation of chat-model VE, its 71%/87% improvement frequencies, and adapted chat models outperforming adapted base models. v3 instead presents ElChat's independence from base models and target chat data as central, with new comparative claims about chat, English, target-language, and safety performance against CV.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations for CV's weaknesses, merging-related safety tradeoffs, and correct-answer/wrong-reasoning failures. Copy changes from an often modest contributor in v1's discussion to a complementary component supported by new chat/reasoning ablations. v3 explicitly qualifies its mainly English chat evaluation, while removing the vocabulary-initialization and model-size limitation paragraphs.

D1.justification: v3 identifies Flow-Judge-v0.1, documents evaluation-framework choices for the new benchmarks, links the safety-evaluation implementation, and expands dataset-license information. Core tokenizer settings, CPT hyperparameters, merging ratios, and hardware details are retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v3 identifies Huang et al.'s Chat Vector as the closest prior work and replaces v1's first-VE-plus-merging positioning with independence from a base model. Related work substantially expands comparisons of data requirements and adaptation strategies, including Geng et al. and examples of unavailable base models.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methodology narrative, results discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around ElChat and CV. Related work moves from Section 7 to Section 2, safety/chat evaluation leads the results, notation is simplified, and v1's takeaway boxes disappear.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is replaced with a CV-versus-ElChat workflow. v3 adds safety/chat plots, MGSM tables, a compact ablation table, and reasoning examples. Existing performance and token-analysis plots are redesigned around fewer models and different comparators, while appendix tables are substantially regrouped and compressed.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important evidential gaps by evaluating the closely related CV method and adding the safety assessment explicitly absent from v1. Direct chat/reasoning benchmarks and component-removal ablations substantially strengthen support for the capabilities the method aims to preserve. These gains outweigh the reduced model and BBH coverage, although the overstated target-task win count in Section 5.2 and remaining English-heavy chat evaluation limit the strength of its broader claims.
